messages:
maria h: FYI I ran a small probe on the KV cache fragmentation problem hitting long-context workloads. found something odd about sparsity + alloc alignment.
aj wong: curious—what did you run exactly?
maria h: short summary: we simulated ~100 concurrent long-chat sessions with synthetic tokens (sequence lengths skewed 8k-12k). enabled compactness sampling and tracked slab occupancy and free-run lengths.
devon k: did you hit the OOM from last week or something different?
maria h: similar symptoms but different root: no single hot prefix overflow. instead many tiny unusable gaps (8–64B) across slabs -> prevents reuse for incoming 2–4KB kv entries. overall mem used grows even though logical entries freed.
aj wong: that sounds like fragmentation by granularity mismatch. is the allocator rounding up too aggressively?
maria h: exactly. our baseline kernel path uses 256B bucketing for small kv items after quant kernel switch. with long ctx, many kv blobs fall between buckets and cause internal slack.
samir: any profiling traces? CPU vs GPU interplay?
maria h: attached a profiler snippet in the logs I pasted:
```
2026-03-15T14:12:03Z shard=5 alloc_size=2048 requested=2020 slab_bucket=256 waste=28
2026-03-15T14:12:03Z evict_candidate=none kv_refcnt=1 free_run_head=64
2026-03-15T14:12:04Z page_walk=30us spill_to_disk=0
```
aj wong: page_walk low but waste adds up across millions of entries. How often are we compacting?
maria h: currently async compact every 60s per shard. compaction only merges contiguous free runs above 1KB, so sub-1KB gaps get left behind.
devon k: can we try adaptive compaction thresholding? like make it proportional to fragmentation ratio not a fixed size.
maria h: proposed experiment: lower compaction threshold to 128B for shards with >12% slack and run canary for 24h. also enable a sparse-coalescer that opportunistically shifts small entries to nearby free runs on write.
samir: what's the perf hit? touching memory shards more often could add CPU and increase latency for hot requests.
maria h: expected CPU delta ~0.8–1.5% in our local sim; worst-case p50 latency bump ~3ms for write-heavy traces. read-heavy long contexts should be mostly unchanged.
aj wong: important to consider kernel selection interaction: if we pick quant kernel path that reduces KV item sizes, bucket distribution changes. Did you test with both kernels?
maria h: yes. two runs: quantized kernel + compacting made fragmentation worse due to smaller but more numerous tiny entries. native fp kernel had fewer but larger entries—less slack.
devon k: interesting. suggests we need a combined mitigation: adjust bucket granularity when on quant kernel OR change batching heuristics to avoid generating many tiny updates.
maria h: implemented a soft fallthrough policy in the runtime: when frag ratio > 20% and compaction backlog > 50MB, route non-critical requests to lower tier or trigger graceful degrade mode (drop KV caching for short-lived sessions).
ops-bot: deploy-check: canary config validated against policies, 3/3 checks passed.
aj wong: can we get telemetry for: frag_ratio, compact_backlog, average_free_run, and kv_reuse_rate per shard? add p99 retention.
maria h: will hook metrics. Also adding a diagnostic trace `kv:compact:decision` that logs why compaction was skipped/ran.
samir: emergency mitigation if we see OOM: 1) increase soft-fallback threshold to 10MB backlog, 2) force immediate compaction on >80% vmem, 3) enable emergency spill-to-disk for oldest prefixes.
devon k: do we have a safe spill path? last time spill overflowed I/O queue and spiked p99.
maria h: new plan: spill is rate-limited by tokens/sec and uses a bounded async queue with backpressure signals to RPC layer. we also added a circuit breaker to disable spill if I/O p99 > 200ms.
aj wong: good. can we run a 6h canary with real traffic pattern (staging capture) and these configs: compact_thresh=128, sparse_coalescer=on, soft_fallback=on, spill_rate_limit=2000req/s?
maria h: scheduled. canary id: kv-sparse-probe-0324. will post results.
ops-bot: canary started: kv-sparse-probe-0324, 5 nodes, duration target 6h.
samir: one more ask: add an experiment toggling batching heuristics—group writes from same session into single write op to reduce small writes. call it `session-write-bunching`. low risk but potentially big win.
maria h: added to canary matrix.
devon k: thanks. if the canary shows stable latencies and reuse_rate improves, we should schedule a staged rollout with monitoring alerts on frag_ratio > 15% and kv_reuse_rate drop > 10 points.
aj wong: agreed. also update runbook: include commands to force compaction and to flip soft-fallback flags.
maria h: runbook snippet:
```
# force compaction shard 5
echo compact > /sys/kv/shard/5/control
# toggle soft fallback
curl -X POST $ADMIN/kv/config -d '{"soft_fallback":true}'
```
maria h: I'll follow up with telemetry dashboards and a short post-canary summary.
aj wong: awesome. keep an eye on any perf regressions from the coalescer.
samir: thanks team, feel free to @pod-leads if we need more nodes for the canary.
maria h: will do. cc: @aj wong for rollout plan.
